extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and national IP office officials operating under the Bangui Agreement / OAPI system
extracted.subtask_short: OAPI patent grant and prosecution rules
extracted.subtask_description: Annex I of the Bangui Agreement setting out definitions, patentability requirements, rights conferred, ownership rules, formal filing requirements, publication, opposition and related procedural rules for patents administered by the Organization (OAPI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Invention' and 'Patent' and excluded subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "Invention" means an idea that permits a specific problem in the field of technology to be solved in practice. "Patent" means the title granted for the protection of an invention. The invention may consist in, or be related to, a product, a process or the use thereof. The following shall not be considered inventions: (a) discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; (b) schemes, principles or methods for doing business, performing purely mental activities or playing games; (c) mere presentation of information; (d) computer programs; (e) purely ornamental creations; and (f) literary, architectural and artistic works or any other esthetic creation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (4) clarifies these exclusions: they 'only exclude the patentability of the enumerated items where the patent application contains one of these items considered as such.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability basic requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: "An invention that is new, involves an inventive step and is industrially applicable may be the subject of an invention patent."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also lists categories that are not patentable despite meeting the three requirements: (a) inventions whose exploitation is contrary to public policy or morality (subject to the caveat that mere prohibition by law does not automatically make it contrary to public policy); (b) methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy, including diagnostic methods; (c) plant varieties, animal species and essentially biological processes for breeding plants or animals (except microbiological processes and products of such processes). Additionally, a substance in the prior art is not excluded from patentability if it is put to a new use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (Article 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An invention shall be new if it has not been anticipated by prior art." Prior art consists of everything made available to the public, anywhere and by any means, before the filing date (or validly claimed priority date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: novelty is not denied if disclosure in the 12 months before the filing/priority date resulted from (a) an obvious violation against the person filing or its author; or (b) display by the applicant/author at an official or officially recognized international exhibition. Also, an earlier application whose filing date is earlier but whose publication was on or after that filing date is part of the prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non‑obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An invention shall be regarded as resulting from an inventive step if, having regard to the prior art, it would not have been obvious to a person having ordinary knowledge and skill in the art on the filing date of the patent application or, if priority has been claimed, on the priority date validly claimed for the application."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard skilled-person (person having ordinary knowledge and skill in the art) non-obviousness test tied to filing/priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An invention shall be considered industrially applicable if its object can be made or used in any kind of industry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'industry' is to be understood in its broadest sense and explicitly includes handicrafts, agriculture, fishery and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the Annex, the patent confers on its owner the exclusive right to work the patented invention and the right to prohibit any person from working the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'working' for product patents (manufacturing, importing, offering for sale, selling, using, and holding for those purposes) and for process patents (using the process and performing product-related acts for products directly obtained by the process). Owner may assign or transfer the patent, enter into contracts. The scope of protection is determined by the claims, with the description and drawings serving to interpret the claims. For process patents, protection encompasses products obtained by the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exceptions to patent rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights conferred by the patent shall not extend to: (a) acts relating to a patented product on a Member State's territory after the product is legally placed on the market by the owner or with his consent (exhaustion); (b) use of objects on board foreign aircraft, land vehicles or ships that temporarily or accidentally enter the territory; (c) acts carried out for experimental purposes in scientific/technical research or for educational purposes; (d) studies and tests required for securing market authorization for medicines and acts necessary for conducting such studies (regulatory/Bolar exception); (e) acts performed by a person who in good faith on the filing or priority date was in possession of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (2) specifies assignment restrictions for the possessor's right and that such rights may be assigned only with the goodwill/establishment to which it is attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: "The patent shall expire at the end of the twentieth calendar year following the filing date of the application," subject to provisions of other Articles (e.g., Articles 30 and 44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard 20-year term measured from filing date; references to other articles for special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to the patent / entitlement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to the patent shall belong to the inventor or his successor in title; the applicant is deemed to be the owner. If several persons create the same invention independently, the right belongs to the person who filed the application with the earliest filing or valid priority date (provided the application is not withdrawn, abandoned or refused). Joint inventors hold the right jointly and the title shall be issued to them as joint owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-to-file rule for independently created identical inventions; joint ownership consequences follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In absence of other provision, joint ownership governed by: (a) each joint owner may work invention to his benefit but must make fair compensation to others not personally working or who have not granted licenses; (b) each joint owner may institute proceedings for counterfeit to his exclusive benefit but must notify others; (c) each joint owner may grant a non‑exclusive license subject to fair compensation and notification procedures (including right of others to acquire the share under specified terms); (d) exclusive exploitation license requires agreement of all joint owners or court leave; (e) assignment of shares permitted with right of first refusal for other joint owners; (f) relinquishment to other joint owners recorded in register relieves relinquishing owner of obligations and share distribution rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural timelines (e.g., three months to challenge/grant/waive, court price fixation if no agreement) and role of competent domestic courts to fix compensation or prices where parties fail to agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees' inventions and commissioned inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the inventor is an employee, absent more favorable contractual provisions: (a) inventions made in performance of an employment contract encompassing an inventive task or expressly assigned studies/research belong to the employer, with supplementary remuneration to employee; (b) inventions made by an employee not required to invent but using employer's techniques/means or information belong to the employee, although employer has the right to be granted ownership or enjoyment of all or part of the rights in return for a fair price; (c) all other inventions belong to the employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employee must immediately inform employer who must acknowledge receipt. Employee-employer agreements must be in writing on pain of invalidity. Provisions apply to public sector employees; domestic law fixes the amount/terms of supplementary remuneration. For commissioned inventions, absent contract provision, right belongs to the client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of patent application into utility model application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patent application that fulfills the conditions stipulated in Annex II as regards utility models may be converted into an application for a utility model. In such case, the patent application shall be deemed to have been withdrawn and the Organization shall enter a 'withdrawn' notice in the Register of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion mechanism for applicants who prefer utility model protection when conditions of Annex II are met; administrative effect is withdrawal and register notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing formalities and contents of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application shall be filed with the Organization or the Ministry responsible for industrial property. The application file shall contain: (a) a patent application addressed to the Director-General in sufficient copies; (b) proof of payment of filing and publication fees; (c) an unstamped private power of attorney if represented by an agent; and (d) a sealed envelope containing: (i) a specification set out clearly and completely so that a person having ordinary knowledge and skill in the art could carry it out; (ii) any necessary drawings; (iii) any claim(s) defining the scope of protection sought which shall not exceed the contents of the specification; (iv) a descriptive abstract; and (v) sufficient indications regarding the best manner of carrying out the invention known to the inventor on the filing date (and priority date, where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes enablement/clear & complete disclosure, claims limited by specification, and requirement to disclose best-known mode/indications available at filing/priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) application procedures and secrecy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall act as a receiving office for international (PCT) applications filed by persons with residence/headquarters in a Member State where priority is not claimed. Inventions the subject of international applications filed with the Organization may not be disclosed and freely worked unless authorization is granted by the Director-General. During that time, applications may not be made public nor certified copies issued without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing regulations shall set the procedure including language, forwarding fees and agent conditions. Authorization to act as receiving office or to disclose may be granted by the Director-General and may be granted at any time. Paragraph (3) lists exceptions (e.g., applicant not resident in Member State, Organization acting on behalf of another national office, or a State designated as receiving office by the Washington Treaty assembly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall grant as the filing date the date of receipt of the application provided that at the time of filing the application contains: (a) an express or implicit indication that the grant of a patent is requested; (b) a part which, at first sight, appears to be the description of an invention and one or more claims; and (c) proof of payment of the prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications, filing date is that assigned by the receiving office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility for non‑payment
rubrics_metrics.description: No application shall be admissible if it is not submitted together with a document noting the payment of the filing fee and the publication fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide proof of fee payment at filing renders the application inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be restricted to a single principal subject, with the details that constitute it and the uses specified. It shall contain no restrictions, conditions or reservations and shall have a title that describes precisely and succinctly the purpose of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-principle requirement — applications must not include unrelated inventions or reservations/conditions; title must be precise and succinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims to priority: time limits and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: To claim priority of an earlier application an applicant must file within 12 months of the earlier filing date. Within six months of filing the application the applicant must attach a written declaration stating the date and number of the earlier application, the country in which it was filed and the name of the filing party; a certified true copy of the earlier application; and if not the original filer, written authorization from the original applicant or successor in title authorizing the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple priorities: comply for each priority and pay a fee per priority (proof of payment within six months). Priority documents received after six months entail loss of the right of priority, though reinstatement may be possible under Article 45; a rejection of reinstatement can be appealed to the High Commission of Appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of patent application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish for each patent application: filing number; filing date; applicant's name and address; inventor's name/address (unless inventor requested not to be mentioned); agent name/address; indication of priorities; priority date/country/number; title; abstract; international application date/number if applicable; and international patent classification symbols. The Organization shall also publish the specifications, claim(s) and any drawings. Publication shall occur within 18 months of the filing date or priority date, save for international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard bibliographic and substantive publication obligations; international applications handled separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition procedure and grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months of publication of the application, any person may oppose the grant of a patent or certificate of addition by submitting a written statement setting out reasons. Reasons must be based on an infringement of the provisions of Articles 2 (patentability), 3 (novelty), 4 (inventive step), 5 (industrial applicability), 9 (right to the patent) or 17 (unity) of this Annex or on a prior registered right belonging to the opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization sends the opposition to the applicant/agent who may submit a reasoned reply within three months (renewable once on application). Before ruling, the Organization shall hear the parties or their agents. (Procedural timelines and right to reply are specified.)
